body:
## Problem

`Client:_get_registrations()` errors if a `documentSelector` pattern is not
a valid glob (e.g. `**/**.dart` from dartls). The error discards
already-matched registrations and propagates to `supports_method()` and
the `client/registerCapability` handler, disabling capabilities unrelated
to the offending pattern.

## Solution

Skip invalid globs. Treat them as non-matching, and log once per client.
(Similar approach was taken for filewatcher globs in #40396.)

Closes #37204

comment_data.body: besides the accidental micro-optimization, does `_glob_cache` exist only to skip the log? sure would be nice if it had a 1-line comment mentioning that.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1058,6 +1060,23 @@ function Client:_get_language_id(bufnr)
   return self.get_language_id(bufnr, vim.bo[bufnr].filetype)
 end
 
+--- @private
+--- @param pattern string
+--- @param fname string
+--- @return boolean
+function Client:_glob_matches(pattern, fname)
+  local pat = self._glob_cache[pattern]

comment_data.body: Both: it skips recompiling on every lookup and ensures each invalid pattern is logged only once per client. Added a comment saying so.

comment_regular_data.body: @barrettruth do you have thoughts here? If we need the same workaround twice, this is possibly a sign?

Both sides of it

- The logging
- having to pcall the glob to work out if it's thrown

> e.g. **/**.dart from dartls

Have you reported this upstream?

> having to pcall the glob to work out if it's thrown

If we choose to handle this (of course we should always push back against these issues at the kernel, the LSP server level), what's wrong with this? Isn't the operation relatively inexpensive?

> > e.g. **/**.dart from dartls
> 
> Have you reported this upstream?

Its fixed in dart specifically (mentioned in the linked issue)

> > having to pcall the glob to work out if it's thrown
> 
> If we choose to handle this (of course we should always push back against these issues at the kernel, the LSP server level), what's wrong with this? Isn't the operation relatively inexpensive?

The reason that that ticket was still open is because it was quite jarring having the LSP client hard error when a server provides a invalid glob, we should handle that gracefully.

its the same error you fixed in the linked PR, but in a different code path

Oh - I thought it was something else, yes of course that's the entire issue XD. Let's wait for justin's input, otherwise @rvaccone take a look at the pattern used [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40396/changes) instead.

Took a look. The difference: in `_watchfiles.lua` globs are parsed once at registration, so only the log needed dedup. Here `_get_registrations` recompiled the glob on every call (it is on the `supports_method` path), so `_glob_cache` is primarily a compile cache and the log dedup falls out of it. It also holds only patterns the server sent in registrations and is freed with the client, unlike the `_watchfiles.lua` set, which outlives clients, so bounding seemed unnecessary. Happy to switch to that pattern or extract one shared helper, whichever is preferred.

> unlike the `_watchfiles.lua` set, which outlives clients, so bounding seemed unnecessary. Happy to switch to that pattern or extract one shared helper, whichever is preferred.

a shared util is usually a good idea, but does `runtime/lua/vim/func/_memoize.lua` already serve the purpose potentially? (i'm lost in the discussion here). or maybe `vim.ringbuf()` is useful, for a bounded cache.

would be great if a solution can be found that avoids maintaining extra state , or else keeps that decision in one place instead of adding more places that maintain caches.

`vim.func._memoize` could work, but only per client with a strong cache. Its default cache is weak, and since nothing else references the cached values, every garbage collection cycle empties it and the invalid pattern logs again. A strong module level cache would instead outlive clients. Either way it is the same state routed through a utility, so I kept the plain cache and added a comment. `vim.ringbuf()` has no keyed lookup.

A no state option: validate documentSelector patterns in `_register_dynamic`, the single entry point for registrations, then log and drop invalid filters there. Dropping a filter has the same effect as today, where an invalid pattern never matches, and the log happens once at registration, so no deduplication state is needed. `_watchfiles.lua` already validates globs at registration. The cost is recompiling globs on every lookup, as before this pull request, and a repeated log if a server resends the same invalid selector. Happy to implement that if preferred.
